## CloudWatch quantification of the Bedrock error blast radius from the 2026-08-10/11 model-comparison runs

An automated ops error sweep pulled AWS/Bedrock metrics (account 896586841071, us-east-1) for 2026-08-05T00:00Z -> 2026-08-12T04:00Z. Posting the numbers here because the errors are **attributable to the model-comparison experiments run under this ticket**, and because they are now fully explained by [rebar:e800-c107-d4ac-463b] (Nova 10k output ceilings), which has since closed and landed on main as f7e684c300.

**InvocationClientErrors by ModelId — the spike:**

| ModelId | 08-10 21:00 PDT | 08-10 22:00 PDT | 08-11 07:00 PDT |
|---|---|---|---|
| us.amazon.nova-pro-v1:0 | 2 | **50** | **16** |
| us.amazon.nova-2-lite-v1:0 | - | 6 | - |
| us.amazon.nova-premier-v1:0 | - | 1 | - |
| us.deepseek.r1-v1:0 | - | 2 | - |

Roughly **77 client errors**, ~94% of them on the Nova family, in a two-hour concentration plus one follow-on hour. This matches e800's account precisely: every Nova call riding the raise-to-model-max seam was rejected with `ValidationException: The maximum tokens you requested exceeds the model limit of 10000` before it ran.

**Two things worth carrying forward for the cost analysis:**

1. **The Claude ladder was essentially untouched** — 1-3 client errors each across the whole week for the opus/sonnet/haiku slots. The `rebar-bedrock-invoke-client-errors` alarm is dimensioned on those three slots only, so it correctly stayed OK throughout. That is the alarm behaving as designed, but it also means **a cheap-model experiment can fail wholesale without any alarm noticing** — worth knowing before this ticket recommends routing real gate traffic to a cheap model.
2. **us.deepseek.r1-v1:0 took 2 client errors and is NOT covered by e800's fix**, which added ceilings for nova-pro / nova-2-lite / nova-lite / nova-micro only. If DeepSeek stays in the candidate set for the lever option book, it likely needs its own ceiling entry. Two errors is thin evidence, so treat this as a flag to check rather than a finding.

**Separately, InvocationServerErrors** (5xx, i.e. Bedrock-side not request-side): 1 on 08-05, 1 on 08-07, then **17 clustered on 2026-08-11 10:00-12:00 PDT**. These are not explained by e800 and are not a rebar defect — but a cost/latency model built from that window should know the provider had a bad two hours in it.

For scale: total Invocations peaked at 48,780 on 2026-08-10, so even the worst error hour is a fraction of a percent of traffic.

Reported by an automated ops error sweep; read-only AWS calls, no code changed.
